item.text: {"question_id":"6B.6","answer":"In 2023, Tshisekedi’s government pursued some crisis-related measures, including a January security-planning meeting with MONUSCO and the EAC force, stated priorities for civilian protection and DDR, the PDL-145T, and free maternity, newborn, family-planning, and education measures with UN cooperation (BATCH-0021-E001; BATCH-0021-E002; BATCH-0010-E006). These passages show governmental planning and reported implementation, but not verified funding, coverage, quality, or crisis-level reductions in suffering. Humanitarian actors delivered substantial food, health, WASH, and protection assistance, including to displaced populations, but the supplied evidence attributes those outputs primarily to UN/ICRC/UNFPA partners and donors rather than to Tshisekedi (BATCH-0013-E015; BATCH-0013-E017; BATCH-0025-E003). The overall crisis remained extremely adverse: more than 6.8–6.9 million people were displaced, over 25 million faced crisis or emergency food insecurity, aid access was uneven, and schools and health services were disrupted (BATCH-0010-E003; BATCH-0013-E014; BATCH-0020-E009; BATCH-0022-E010). Ruler-linked protection performance was especially weak: authorities delayed reinforcement and failed to provide adequate assistance after Kwamouth displacement, while the state of siege—continued and repeatedly extended by the government despite its stated civilian-protection purpose—coincided with worsening security, increasing civilian casualties, and serious rights abuses (BATCH-0011-E001; BATCH-0012-R03-E004). The planned and state-authorized Goma operation further resulted in at least 56 deaths, with a higher confidential UN estimate, injuries, arbitrary arrests, and inadequate accountability procedures, although the evidence does not establish a direct presidential order for the killings (BATCH-0011-E018). Armed-group violence, regional conflict, donor shortfalls, and limited state capacity materially constrain causal attribution, but they do not erase the documented government-level delays, policy failures, and protection harms (BATCH-0016-E004; BATCH-0016-E005; BATCH-0020-E010).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0021-E002","BATCH-0010-E006","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0025-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0020-E009","BATCH-0022-E010","BATCH-0011-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E004","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0016-E004","BATCH-0016-E005","BATCH-0020-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not establish national counterfactuals or quantify how much suffering was reduced by government measures.","Reported social-service and humanitarian outputs lack reliable national coverage, uptake, funding, quality, and distribution data.","Several favorable outputs were implemented by UN, ICRC, UNFPA, or other partners, so attribution to Tshisekedi is limited.","The evidence does not establish a direct presidential order for the Goma killings, and conflict-related outcomes have multiple causes."],"corrections_made":["Removed ICC cooperation as irrelevant to direct crisis-preparedness or suffering-reduction evidence.","Reframed MONUSCO and humanitarian operations as external or jointly supported actions rather than direct presidential achievements.","Gave greater weight and specificity to delayed Kwamouth assistance, state-of-siege failure, and the Goma operation.","Separated governmental plans and reported measures from verified implementation and attributable outcomes."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if evidence of government emergency funding, coverage, implementation quality, or corrective action becomes available.","Reopen if comparable baseline or counterfactual evidence clarifies the government’s contribution to displacement, food insecurity, or crisis-service outcomes."]}
